sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: This visa stream is for citizens from certain areas of China visiting Australia on a tour organised by an approved travel agent.

sections.heading: Overview > You must:
sections.text:
- be a citizen of the People’s Republic of China
- intend to travel to Australia as part of a tour organised by an approved travel agent
- contact an approved travel agent to ask for them to apply for this visa on your behalf. For more information, see our Step by step guide.

sections.heading: Overview > With this visa you can
sections.text: - visit Australia as part of a tour group

sections.heading: Overview > How long you can stay
sections.text: For the period or until the date we specify in your grant letter

sections.heading: Overview > Processing time
sections.text:
For an indication of processing times for this visa, use the visa processing time guide tool. This will show the processing times for recently decided applications. It is a guide only and not specific to your application.

Visa processing times are based on the age of applications finalised in a given period. Many applications finalised recently had been on-hand for some months while borders were closed.

For more information see visa processing times.

sections.heading: About this visa > With this visa you can
sections.text:
- can enter Australia with your approved tour group
- can participate in activities that are part of your tour
- must leave Australia with your tour group before your visa expires

sections.heading: About this visa > How long you can stay
sections.text:
This is a temporary visa. If we grant you a visa we will let you know how long you can stay in your visa grant letter. We consider the length of your tour when we determine your stay period.

We grant the visa with either:

- single entry. If you leave Australia you will have to apply for another visa to come back
- multiple entry. You can leave and re-enter Australia on this visa while it is valid

sections.heading: About this visa > Include family
sections.text:
You can't include family members in your application. A separate application must be made for each member of your family, including those listed on your passport.

Newborn child

Find out what to do if your child is born after you apply.

sections.heading: About this visa > Cost
sections.text:
The visa costs .

You might also have to pay other costs for health checks, police certificates and biometrics.

Use the Visa Pricing Estimator to work out what your visa will cost. The estimator does not take into account the other costs.

sections.heading: About this visa > Apply from
sections.text: You must be in the People's Republic of China when your visa application is lodged and when we make a decision on your application.

sections.heading: About this visa > Processing times
sections.text: For an indication of processing times for this visa, use the visa processing time guide tool. This will show the processing times for recently decided applications. It is a guide only and not specific to your application.

sections.heading: About this visa > Your obligations
sections.text: You must meet all visa conditions and obey Australian laws.

sections.heading: About this visa > Health insurance
sections.text:
We recommend you take out health insurance to cover any unforeseen medical treatment you might need in Australia. You are personally liable for all your healthcare costs while you are in Australia. Insurance can help limit your financial liability.

See what we consider adequate health insurance.

Learn more about health insurance for overseas visitors.

Reciprocal healthcare agreements

Some countries have a reciprocal healthcare agreement with Australia. Find out more from Services Australia about reciprocal healthcare agreements.

sections.heading: About this visa > Visa label
sections.text: We will digitally link your visa to your passport. You will not get a label in your passport.

sections.heading: Eligibility
sections.text: You must meet all of these criteria to be eligible for the Visitor visa Approved Destination Status stream.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Meet our character requirement
sections.text: You must meet our character requirement.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have repaid debt to the Australian Government
sections.text: If you or any family members (including those who don't apply for the visa with you) owe the Australian government money, you or they must have paid it back or arranged to pay it back.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Be a genuine visitor
sections.text:
You must only intend to:

- stay temporarily in Australia
- obey any condition and stay period attached to your visa

sections.heading: Eligibility > Best interests of the child
sections.text: We might not grant this visa if it is not in the best interests of an applicant under 18.

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply > Organise health exams
sections.text:
You might need to have health examinations. You can complete them before you apply or you can wait until we tell you to have them.

Find out the examinations you need and how to arrange them if you want to have them before you apply.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Provide accurate information
sections.text:
Provide accurate information.

See what happens if you can't prove your identity or don't provide true information.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Identity documents
sections.text:
Provide the pages of your current People's Republic of China passport showing your photo, personal details, and passport issue and expiry dates.

Also provide:

- a national identity card, if you have one
- proof of change of name

Documents that prove a change of name include:

- a marriage or divorce certificate
- change of name documents from an Australian Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, or the relevant overseas authority
- documents that show other names you have been known by

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Additional documents for applicants 75 years old or older
sections.text:
Provide:

- evidence of health insurance to cover your stay in Australia
- your Yellow Book

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Additional documents for applicants under 18
sections.text:
You must get consent for any applicant under 18 years of age to migrate to Australia from anyone who:

- has a legal right to decide where the child lives and
- is not coming to Australia with the child

They must complete either:

- Form 1229 Consent form to grant an Australian visa to a child under the age of 18 years
- a statutory declaration giving their consent for the child to visit Australia on this visa

Alternatively, you can show us:

- an Australian court order that allows your child to migrate to Australia, or
- that the laws of your home country allow them to migrate

Include:

- an identity document that shows the signature and photo of the person who completed the form or declaration, such as a passport or driver’s licence
- adoption papers or other court documents if applicable

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents
sections.text:
Translate

Have all non-English documents translated into English.

Provide original and translated documents in your application.

Translators in Australia must be accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters.

Translators outside Australia do not have to be accredited. But on each translation, they must include their:

- full name
- address and telephone number
- qualifications and experience in the language they are translating

These details must be in English.

You do not need to have any documents certified unless we ask you to.

sections.heading: Step by step > Apply for the visa
sections.text:
You need to contact a registered Approved Destination Status scheme travel agent to ask for them to apply for this visa on your behalf. Your travel agent must be registered with the Approved Destination Status scheme.

Provide accurate information

See what happens if you can't prove your identity or don't provide true information.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > What will happen after you apply
sections.text:
We will let you know when we have received your application and documents.

There are other things you need to know and might need to do.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Travel
sections.text: Don't make arrangements to travel to Australia until you know you have been granted the visa.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Health exams
sections.text: If you did not have health examinations before you applied, we will let you know if you need them.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Send more information
sections.text:
If you did not send us all documents when you applied, send them as soon as you can.

We might also ask you to provide more information.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Mistakes on your application
sections.text: Let your travel agent know as soon as you can if you made a mistake on your application.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Tell us if things change
sections.text:
Tell your travel agent if things change after you lodge your application but before we have made a decision.

Things you need to let them know about include:

- you want to withdraw your application
- changes to your phone number, address or passport
- changes to your relationship status
- the birth of a child

sections.heading: Step by step > Visa outcome
sections.text:
We will let your travel agent know our decision about your visa application. We will send them a visa grant letter with:

- your visa grant number
- the date your visa starts
- your visa conditions

You might like to get a copy of the letter to keep with you when in Australia.

If we refuse your visa we will let you know by email. We will tell you why we refused and whether you have a right to a review of the decision.

We will not refund the application fee if we refuse your application.

Step Summary

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Coming to Australia
sections.text:
Before you travel

Check your travel documents

You must have:

- a valid visa to enter Australia
- a valid passport or other travel document

At the border

Complete an Incoming Passenger Card

Everyone who arrives in Australia must complete an Incoming Passenger Card.

Using the SmartGate

A SmartGate is an automated process that uses facial recognition technology and your ePassport. You might be able to leave the airport faster if you use the SmartGate.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > In Australia
sections.text:
What you must do on your visa

You must stay with your tour group.

You must meet all visa conditions and obey Australian laws. See your conditions in VEVO or your visa grant letter.

Learn more about visa conditions and how they work.

What you can do on your visa

With this visa you:

- can enter Australia with your approved tour group
- can participate in activities that are part of your tour
- must leave Australia with your tour group before your visa expires

To see your specific conditions, work and study entitlements use VEVO.

Stay longer

You can't stay in Australia longer by extending this visa. You must leave Australia with your tour group at the time listed in your tour itinerary.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Leaving Australia
sections.text:
Before you leave

Check your travel documents

You must have a valid passport or other travel document to leave Australia.

At the border

Departures SmartGate

We have an automated process that uses facial recognition technology and your ePassport. You might be able to leave the airport faster if you use SmartGate.

After you leave

International Movement Record

Request your international movement records to get proof of your travel in and out of Australia.

sections.text: - You need to be holding a subclass 457 visa

sections.heading: Sponsor > Overview > How long you can stay
sections.text: This is a permanent visa. You can stay in Australia indefinitely
